settings.headline: Shop numbing cream by strength.
settings.body: Clinical is the baseline most appointments call for. Advanced is the higher strength for longer or more sensitive work. Professional is the highest strength, developed with practitioners, for the most demanding sessions. Choose your size on each card.

settings.headline: When cream is the right format.
settings.body: Cream is the precise format — a layer applied to clean skin and held in place while it takes effect. It suits the broadest range of aesthetic appointments: smaller, defined areas and the bookings most people make. Where the work runs longer or over larger areas, gel and spray each have their place.

settings.headline: Two more formats sit alongside cream.
settings.body: Gel suits sustained work like microneedling; spray suits the body and broader areas.

settings.question: Which numbing cream strength do I need?
settings.answer: Clinical is the baseline most appointments call for. Advanced is the higher strength for longer or more sensitive work. Professional is the highest strength, developed with practitioners, for the most demanding sessions.

settings.question: What is the strongest numbing cream?
settings.answer: Professional is the highest strength in the Senseless system — the strongest we make, available without restriction. Most appointments are well served by Clinical, with Advanced for longer or more sensitive work.

settings.question: How long before my appointment should I apply it?
settings.answer: As a general guide, around 45–60 minutes ahead. It varies with the product and the appointment, so follow the product guidance and your practitioner.

settings.question: How long does it last?
settings.answer: It comes down to three things: the strength you've chosen, how well it was applied — a thick layer, covered, left long enough — and how long and demanding the appointment is. Coverage fades gradually rather than stopping suddenly, so matching the strength to the appointment is what keeps it lasting as long as you need.

settings.question: Do I need to patch test?
settings.answer: Yes — a small amount 24 hours ahead, on the wrist or behind the ear. If there's any reaction, don't use it.

settings.question: Is this a medicine?
settings.answer: No. A UK cosmetic product, not a medicine.
